fixes.explanation: Correct, friend. Verse 20 says that if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed. The door closes, and there's no knocking on it afterward. It's like a cookie sale where the last batch sells out and you're standing there with an empty box, still saying, "But I wanted one!" So the time to buy it back is while he still can.

I know, friend, it sounds like a trick question. A field going to the priests? But read it slowly. Leviticus 27:21 says that when the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD, and it becomes the property of the priests. This is the field from verse 20, which was not redeemed, or was sold to another man. So the statement is True, and the text says it plainly.
